# tlaup command-line reference

## `tlaup`

```text
tlaup [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Install and pin TLA+ tools, compile Java overrides, and run TLC with readable output

Options:

- `--version, -V`: Show the application's version and exit.
- `--debug`: Show the full traceback when an error occurs.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

Run:

- `tlc`: Run the TLC model checker on a TLA+ specification.
- `sany`: Parse a TLA+ specification with SANY and print its errors.
- `pcal`: Translate the PlusCal algorithm of a spec to TLA+ with the PlusCal translator.
- `repl`: Start the TLA+ REPL of the pinned build (rolling builds only).

Manage:

- `tool`: Install, pin and remove TLA+ tools builds (tla2tools.jar).
- `module`: Manage your own TLA+ modules, with optional Java operator overrides.
- `config`: Show and change tlaup's settings.
- `cache`: Show and clean what tlaup keeps in its cache folder.

Maintenance:

- `doctor`: Check the setup tlaup relies on, one line per check.
- `completion`: Print the completion script of a shell.

### `tlaup tlc`

```text
tlaup tlc [OPTIONS] {SPEC} [-- TLC ARGS]...
```

Run the TLC model checker on a TLA+ specification.

Arguments:

- `SPEC`: A TLA+ spec: a name (`Spec`), a file (`Spec.tla`) or a path. `spec/Spec.tla` is tried too.
  (required)
- `-- TLC ARGS...`: TLC's own arguments, after `--`: tlaup tlc Spec -- -deadlock. Relative paths
  after `--` are read from the folder you run tlaup in, -config from the spec's folder; absolute
  paths are advised.

Options:

- `--cfg FILE`: The model's .cfg file, a name or a path (default: TLC's own, Spec.cfg beside the
  spec).
- `--workers N|auto`: The number of TLC workers, or auto for one per core (default: the setting
  tlc.workers).
- `--coverage`: Report how often each action and expression was evaluated.
- `--raw`: Print TLC's own output unchanged, with no parsing or formatting. On Windows a closed
  output pipe does not stop TLC.
- `--plain`: Plain output on a terminal too: each line as it arrives, no live view (default: the
  setting tlc.plain). No effect with --raw.
- `--refresh-interval SECONDS`: How often the live view is redrawn, in seconds (default: the setting
  tlc.refresh_interval, 1.0). No effect with plain output or --raw.
- `--keep`: Keep the run folder when the run is interrupted or crashes after a complete checkpoint.
- `--show-command`: Print the command that would run, and run nothing. The printed command does not
  stop TLC when the terminal that pasted it is killed; for a long run pasted by hand, replace the
  -metadir value with a folder of your own.
- `--java-opt OPT`: An option for the JVM, repeatable: --java-opt=-Xmx8g.
- `--auto-install stable|rolling`: With no tools installed, install this build without asking:
  stable or rolling.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

```text
Examples:

tlaup tlc Spec

tlaup tlc Spec --workers auto --cfg Spec.cfg

tlaup tlc Spec -- -deadlock
```

### `tlaup sany`

```text
tlaup sany [OPTIONS] {SPEC} [-- SANY ARGS]...
```

Parse a TLA+ specification with SANY and print its errors.

Arguments:

- `SPEC`: A TLA+ spec: a name (`Spec`), a file (`Spec.tla`) or a path. `spec/Spec.tla` is tried too.
  SANY reads it from the spec's own folder, and looks for modules in the spec's folder, then the
  library folders, then the standard modules, then the classpath. (required)
- `-- SANY ARGS...`: SANY's own arguments, after `--`: tlaup sany Spec -- -stat. `-d` is refused: it
  starts an explorer that waits for input; run it with Java directly on the jar that `tlaup tool
  path` prints.

Options:

- `--java-opt OPT`: An option for the JVM, repeatable: --java-opt=-Xmx8g.
- `--auto-install stable|rolling`: With no tools installed, install this build without asking:
  stable or rolling.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

```text
Examples:

tlaup sany Spec

tlaup sany Spec -- -stat
```

### `tlaup pcal`

```text
tlaup pcal [OPTIONS] {SPEC} [-- TRANSLATOR ARGS]...
```

Translate the PlusCal algorithm of a spec to TLA+ with the PlusCal translator.

Arguments:

- `SPEC`: A TLA+ spec: a name (`Spec`), a file (`Spec.tla`) or a path. `spec/Spec.tla` is tried too.
  The spec is rewritten in place and the previous version is kept as SPEC.old; SPEC.cfg is written,
  or rewritten with no backup (pass `-- -nocfg` to leave it alone). The translator reads the spec
  from the spec's own folder. (required)
- `-- TRANSLATOR ARGS...`: The translator's own arguments, after `--`: tlaup pcal Spec -- -nocfg.

Options:

- `--java-opt OPT`: An option for the JVM, repeatable: --java-opt=-Xmx8g.
- `--auto-install stable|rolling`: With no tools installed, install this build without asking:
  stable or rolling.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `tlaup repl`

```text
tlaup repl [OPTIONS] [-- ARGS]...
```

Start the TLA+ REPL of the pinned build (rolling builds only).

Ctrl-C belongs to the REPL, and SIGTERM stops it from outside. The REPL keeps its history in
~/.tlaplus/history.repl, where upstream puts it.

Arguments:

- `-- ARGS...`: The REPL's own arguments, after `--`: tlaup repl -- ARGS.

Options:

- `--java-opt OPT`: An option for the JVM, repeatable: --java-opt=-Xmx8g.
- `--auto-install stable|rolling`: With no tools installed, install this build without asking:
  stable or rolling.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `tlaup tool`

```text
tlaup tool [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Install, pin and remove TLA+ tools builds (tla2tools.jar).

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

Commands:

- `list`: List the TLA+ tools releases that have a jar.
- `install`: Download and install a TLA+ tools build.
- `upgrade`: Replace an installed version with the newest build of the same name.
- `uninstall`: Remove installed TLA+ tools builds.
- `pin`: Pin the TLA+ tools build that runs use.
- `current`: Show the pinned TLA+ tools build and the path of its jar, without starting Java.
- `path`: Print the path of a TLA+ tools build's jar.
- `dir`: Print the folder that holds the installed TLA+ tools builds.

#### `tlaup tool list`

```text
tlaup tool list [OPTIONS]
```

List the TLA+ tools releases that have a jar.

Newest first with rolling at the top, each followed by its installed builds.

Options:

- `--installed`: List the installed builds only, without asking GitHub.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup tool install`

```text
tlaup tool install [OPTIONS] [VERSION]
```

Download and install a TLA+ tools build.

With no VERSION, asks whether to install `stable` or `rolling`. The first build installed is pinned.

Arguments:

- `VERSION`: A tag such as v1.7.4 or 1.7.4, stable, rolling, or tag@commit for one build.

Options:

- `--force`: Download the build again even when it is installed, and repair it in place.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

```text
Examples:

tlaup tool install stable

tlaup tool install v1.7.4

tlaup tool install rolling --force
```

#### `tlaup tool upgrade`

```text
tlaup tool upgrade [OPTIONS] [VERSION]
```

Replace an installed version with the newest build of the same name.

Rolling builds are rebuilt often; this fetches the current one. It does not move to a different
version: use `install` for that.

Arguments:

- `VERSION`: The name to upgrade, such as rolling, stable or v1.8.0; with none, the pinned build's
  name.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup tool uninstall`

```text
tlaup tool uninstall [OPTIONS] [VERSION]...
```

Remove installed TLA+ tools builds.

A VERSION that matches several builds asks which on a terminal, and removes all of them with --yes
or without a terminal.

Arguments:

- `VERSION...`: The builds to remove: a tag, stable, rolling, or tag@commit for one build.

Options:

- `--all`: Remove every installed build.
- `--yes`: Answer every question of this command with yes.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup tool pin`

```text
tlaup tool pin [OPTIONS] {VERSION}
```

Pin the TLA+ tools build that runs use.

A VERSION that matches several builds asks which on a terminal.

Arguments:

- `VERSION`: An installed build: a tag such as v1.7.4 or 1.7.4, stable, rolling, or tag@commit.
  (required)

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup tool current`

```text
tlaup tool current [OPTIONS]
```

Show the pinned TLA+ tools build and the path of its jar, without starting Java.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup tool path`

```text
tlaup tool path [OPTIONS] [VERSION]
```

Print the path of a TLA+ tools build's jar.

It prints the pinned build's, or the one VERSION names. It never asks.

Arguments:

- `VERSION`: An installed build: a tag such as v1.7.4 or 1.7.4, stable, rolling, or tag@commit.
  Without it, the pinned build.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup tool dir`

```text
tlaup tool dir [OPTIONS]
```

Print the folder that holds the installed TLA+ tools builds.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `tlaup module`

```text
tlaup module [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Manage your own TLA+ modules, with optional Java operator overrides.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

Commands:

- `add`: Build a module folder and register it under the folder's name.
- `list`: List the registered modules with the time each was built, in UTC.
- `remove`: Remove a registered module by name.
- `dir`: Print the folder that holds the registered modules.

#### `tlaup module add`

```text
tlaup module add [OPTIONS] {PATH}
```

Build a module folder and register it under the folder's name.

The folder holds the module's TLA+ files in `modules/*.tla`, its Java operator overrides in
`modules/tlc2/overrides/*.java` or `tlc2/overrides/*.java`, and its jars in `lib/*.jar`. The
folder's name becomes the module's name. An existing module of that name is replaced.

Arguments:

- `PATH`: The module's folder, laid out as above. (required)

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

```text
Examples:

tlaup module add Queue

tlaup module add path/to/Queue
```

#### `tlaup module list`

```text
tlaup module list [OPTIONS]
```

List the registered modules with the time each was built, in UTC.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup module remove`

```text
tlaup module remove [OPTIONS] {NAME}
```

Remove a registered module by name.

Arguments:

- `NAME`: The name of a registered module, as `tlaup module list` shows it. (required)

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup module dir`

```text
tlaup module dir [OPTIONS]
```

Print the folder that holds the registered modules.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `tlaup config`

```text
tlaup config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Show and change tlaup's settings.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

Commands:

- `path`: Print the path of the config file, whether or not it exists.
- `show`: Print the settings in effect as YAML.
- `get`: Print one setting, in the form `config set` reads it.
- `set`: Set one setting in the config file.
- `edit`: Open the config file in $VISUAL or $EDITOR, then check it.

#### `tlaup config path`

```text
tlaup config path [OPTIONS]
```

Print the path of the config file, whether or not it exists.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup config show`

```text
tlaup config show [OPTIONS]
```

Print the settings in effect as YAML.

Each setting comes with the layer it came from: default, user file or environment.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup config get`

```text
tlaup config get [OPTIONS] {KEY}
```

Print one setting, in the form `config set` reads it.

Arguments:

- `KEY`: A setting, as section.name (tlc.workers); `config show` lists them. (required)

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup config set`

```text
tlaup config set [OPTIONS] {KEY} {VALUE}
```

Set one setting in the config file.

Rewrites the config file. Comments in it are not kept; use `tlaup config edit` to keep them.

Arguments:

- `KEY`: A setting, as section.name (tlc.workers); `config show` lists them. (required)
- `VALUE`: The new value, read as YAML: 4, auto, true, or '\[ghe.example.com]' for a list. Quote it
  for the shell. (required)

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup config edit`

```text
tlaup config edit [OPTIONS]
```

Open the config file in $VISUAL or $EDITOR, then check it.

Give the editor's wait flag, as in EDITOR='code --wait'; an editor that returns at once leaves
nothing to check.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `tlaup cache`

```text
tlaup cache [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Show and clean what tlaup keeps in its cache folder.

The folder holds run folders, remembered lookups and the Java check.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

Commands:

- `dir`: Print the cache folder, whether or not it exists.
- `list`: List the run folders, then the total of the kept ones.
- `clean`: Remove what nothing will use again.

#### `tlaup cache dir`

```text
tlaup cache dir [OPTIONS]
```

Print the cache folder, whether or not it exists.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup cache list`

```text
tlaup cache list [OPTIONS]
```

List the run folders, then the total of the kept ones.

A row has the id, spec, build, when the run started and last changed, size, whether it is in use,
whether it is kept and why, and whether its checkpoint is complete.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

#### `tlaup cache clean`

```text
tlaup cache clean [OPTIONS] [RUN_ID]
```

Remove what nothing will use again.

That is run folders that no run holds and that are not kept, and the remembered GitHub lookups. A
kept run folder, and one that asked to be kept and holds a complete checkpoint, stay unless --all or
its RUN_ID says so. A run folder in use is never removed. It never touches installed tools or
modules.

Arguments:

- `RUN_ID`: Remove this one run folder, kept or not, if no run holds it (`cache list` shows the
  ids).

Options:

- `--runs`: Clean run folders only (and their stale lock files).
- `--remote`: Clean the remembered GitHub lookups only.
- `--all`: Widen what is cleaned: with --runs, kept and resumable run folders too; with --remote, no
  change; with no kind named, both of those and the remembered Java check.
- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `tlaup doctor`

```text
tlaup doctor [OPTIONS]
```

Check the setup tlaup relies on, one line per check.

It checks Java, javac, the pinned build, the config file and the folders tlaup uses, and prints ok,
warning or error for each. It re-runs the Java version checks and rewrites the remembered answers.
Exits 3 when a check is an error. It makes no request and changes nothing else.

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.

### `tlaup completion`

```text
tlaup completion [OPTIONS] {SHELL}
```

Print the completion script of a shell.

Put one line in the shell's start-up file: eval "$(tlaup completion bash)" in ~/.bashrc, eval
"$(tlaup completion zsh)" in ~/.zshrc (after compinit), tlaup completion fish | source in
~/.config/fish/config.fish. Installed versions, module names and config keys are completed. In bash
a build is completed up to its name; the part after @ is typed.

Arguments:

- `SHELL`: The shell: bash, zsh or fish. (required)

Options:

- `--help`: Show this message and exit.
